text:
nina: Quick thought — we need a focused follow-up on routing churn when a region hits transient 5xx. Simulation idea to measure policy oscillation vs graceful degradation.
kevin: +1. Are we measuring policy graph recompute frequency or the runtime's affinity timers? both matter.
sam: I prototyped a small harness last week. It toggles region penalties and injects ephemeral capacity drops. output looked like oscillations every ~12s.
marie: do we have the config used? can we run under the real policy engine instead of the mock?
sam: posted snippet: ```json
{"sim_steps":500, "penalty_decay":0.1, "recompute_interval_ms":5000, "min_lease_ms":15000}
```
kevin: that recompute interval seems low. If two controllers recompute at different offsets you get flip-flopping. we should add jitter and a leader-bounded window.
marie: agree. Also consider separating "stability decisions" from "routing weight updates". keep the former coarse-grained, the latter can be interpolated.
ops: note: ops-bot flagged region-eu1 with a short 503 burst at 12:06 UTC today, could reproduce.
routebot: incident detected: eu1 503 spike (12:06) — affected 2k reqs, mean P95 latency spike 350ms.
nina: proposal: policy-engine change set — (1) introduce 'settling_window_ms' (default 30s) for any penalty change before applying to weights, (2) add "soft_penalty" that decays but doesn't immediately zero-out, (3) add optional per-tenant override to prefer regional affinity.
sam: sounds reasonable. settling_window will reduce churn but increases failover time. tradeoff: SLO vs stability. we should quantify.
kevin: we need fallback experiments: simulate high-latency vs high-error. sometimes you want immediate failover on 5xx, sometimes prefer slower degraded mode. maybe make failover mode policy-configurable by class (latency-sensitive vs eventually-consistent).
marie: interface question: how do we surface these controls in the policy DSL? new top-level keys? suggestion: add `stability:{window_ms, decay_alpha, failover_mode}` to the policy node. keeps it explicit and versionable.
nina: also ops concern: state sync. right now each runtime caches resolved weights with TTL=5s. we should consider hierarchical invalidation: controller issues invalidation token which forces immediate recompute when set.
kevin: +1 for invalidation token. but be careful: token storms (many tenants) will cause recompute thundering. add token backoff and controller-side coalescing.
marie: testing plan: (A) offline sim harness that varies recompute_interval and settling_window across a grid and captures churn metrics (switch rate, avg latency, outage windows) (B) canary rollout with `settling_window=30s` on 10% traffic for a week with synthetic failures injected.
sam: for metrics, track: policy_switches_per_minute, avg_weight_entropy, percent_requests_routed_to_degraded_model, customer_error_rate_delta.
nina: nice list. I'll write a short RFC follow-up with these items and the sim config. target for PR: next Wed.
ops: slack note — when we run canary, please tag #incidents and set on-call notify so we can catch regressions early. :eyes:
kevin: one final thought — consider a mode that uses "graceful fallback slots" where a small fraction of requests always probe lower-tier regions to keep KV caches warm. reduces cold-start penalty on failover.
marie: love that. add to RFC as optional optimization (probing_pct, probe_rate_limit).
nina: cool, thanks everyone. I'll draft RFC and attach sim results.
routebot: RFC draft created: https://redwood/internal/rfcs/1234 — Nina.
marie: ack, will review.
